data.title: Real NASA Data
data.lead: Every fact and storm the game shows comes from a saved file or a checked page. Labels tell you how fresh the file is.
data.pagesLead: Partner pages (for example Canadian Space Agency) are marked. Links open in a new tab.
data.failed: This fetch did not return usable data, so the game does not show it.
data.honest1: Live NASA data: only if a live feed is wired. This build never claims live.
data.honest2: NASA data updated …: from data/latest.json, refreshed by the weekly script.
data.honest3: Saved NASA data from …: from the archive file data/storms.json.
data.honest4: Training alert: a practice storm when no usable NASA events are on disk.
data.use.donki: Solar flares and particle events shape the in-game storm.
data.use.osdr: A regolith plant study supports a greenhouse research line.
data.use.radlab: One space radiation reading can appear on the storm card.
data.detail.donki: Weekly file: {latest} usable events (fetched {latestDate}). Archive: {saved} usable events (saved {savedDate}).
teach.title: For teachers and parents
teach.lead: Luna Crew is a short classroom mission. Kids plan work points, meet a solar storm built from saved NASA data, and hear why Earth is a special home.
teach.learn1: Share limited work points across power, life support, shield and science.
teach.learn2: See that night on the Moon means no sunlight for panels and extra heater use.
teach.learn3: Meet a solar storm labeled as updated, saved or training data.
teach.learn4: Read short, sourced facts about air, water, plants and space weather.
teach.use1: A full mission is {rounds} rounds across {days} lunar days. Plan about 20 to 30 minutes.
teach.use2: Turn on practice in crew setup for a guided first round.
teach.use3: Use ?demo=1 to bring the storm earlier for a short demo.
teach.use4: English and Japanese share the same buttons. Switch language any time in Settings.
teach.real1: Storm dates, flare classes and source links come from NASA DONKI files saved in the repo.
teach.real2: Mission Card answers and fact chips always name a checked https source.
teach.real3: Bar numbers and work points are game units for learning, not real mission quantities.
teach.talk1: Why did Power drop more at night?
teach.talk2: When is shelter the safer choice than keeping work going?
teach.talk3: What does Earth give us that a Moon base must make or bring?
teach.access1: Sound, motion, text size and high contrast live in Settings.
teach.access2: Keyboard focus stays inside open dialogs. Escape closes dismissible ones.
teach.access3: Color is never the only signal: icons mark every bar and job.
settings.soundHint: Soft beeps made in the browser. No audio files.
settings.motionHint: Less animation for the scene and typing.
